Number of studies.evidence_source: Across the two studies, there is initial support for the importance of guilt as a key process through which appearance goals for exercise are associated with body image. Study 1 provides crosssectional evidence for the shared variation in appearance goals, introjected regulation, and body image, assessing all three within a single model, while controlling for other regulations and goals. The experimental manipulation of these variables within Study 2 provides support for the proposition that guilt relating to exercise may result in increased body anxiety, in spite of the limitations discussed previously.

section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the findings from two studies, Study 1 and Study 2, focusing on the role of guilt in the association between appearance goals for exercise and body image. Study 1 provided cross-sectional evidence, while Study 2 used an experimental manipulation. The discussion highlights introjected regulation as a key pathway linking appearance goals and negative body image, particularly in female undergraduate students in the UK, and suggests future research directions.
section_summary.evidence_source: Across the two studies, there is initial support for the importance of guilt as a key process through which appearance goals for exercise are associated with body image. Study 1 provides crosssectional evidence for the shared variation in appearance goals, introjected regulation, and body image, assessing all three within a single model, while controlling for other regulations and goals. The experimental manipulation of these variables within Study 2 provides support for the proposition that guilt relating to exercise may result in increased body anxiety, in spite of the limitations discussed previously. In addition to methodological issues relating to the individual studies, previously discussed, the nature of the sample limits the extent to which its findings can be generalized beyond female undergraduate students in the UK.
